subject: CedarBridge capacity plan — GPU provisioning hedge & p95 safety
messages:
From: Olivia Park <opark@cedarbridge.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: CedarBridge Sales <sales@cedarbridge.com>
Date: 2026-06-13T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial throughput surface area & requirements for Dedicated POC

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team liked Redwood’s fallback routing and the pre-warming options. To help move the Dedicated PO C forward, attached is a sample token profile (CSV) extracted from a 2-week production trace for our user-facing summarization endpoint. High level: average sequence length ~420 tokens, ~40% of requests are short (<64 tokens), peak hourly TPS seen in our test window was 110 requests/sec with a mean of ~62 requests/sec.

Key asks for you:
- Please confirm a tokens/sec estimation we should use to size a 99.9% availability slab for our target P95 latency of <350ms (for the medium prompt class).
- We also want a recommended headroom factor (percent) to protect against bursty traffic during weekly batch imports.

Can you loop in the provisioning folks and provide a rough MPP (max tokens/sec) -> GPU slab mapping? We’re targeting a July 1 pilot start.

Thanks,
Olivia Park
Senior Product Ops, CedarBridge

Attachments: CedarBridge_Token_Profiles.csv
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-06-13T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial throughput surface area & requirements for Dedicated POC

Ben / Kim / Vivek — forwarding CedarBridge token profile. Olivia asked for a tokens/sec -> slab mapping and a headroom recommendation for P95 <350ms.

Quick notes from initial pass:
- Their avg seq len (~420) with 40% shorts will skew batching benefits; we should model three buckets (short, medium, long).
- Model variant: they confirmed they plan to use an Llama-3-70B-like family (dense) with 8-bit quantized runtime option. That materially changes per-token throughput.
- Cold starts: they may have weekly imports that will temporarily disable effective KV cache; include a cold-start multiplier.

Kim — can you run a micro-simulation (ppt or spreadsheet) mapping tokens/sec to effective TPS under our quantized runtime; assume 30% latency uplift in cold-cache windows. Ben/Vivek — what's a conservative headroom percent you would require for a committable slab (monthly) vs a burst-capable reservation?

I’ll coordinate a short call with CedarBridge if we need clarifications.

Thanks,
Mateo

(Attachment: forwarded CedarBridge_Token_Profiles.csv)
From: Kim Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Olivia Park <opark@cedarbridge.com>
Date: 2026-06-14T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial throughput surface area & requirements for Dedicated POC — draft MPP spreadsheet

All — draft estimates below (high-level; I attached an MPP workbook to the Drive link in the thread).

Assumptions:
- Model family baseline: dense 70B, 8-bit quantized, inference runtime at TPU-equivalent latency profile on A100-class GPU with our optimized kernels.
- Effective tokens/sec per GPU (warm, cached KV): ~9,200 tok/s (mixed seq distribution).
- Cold-cache penalty: assume 30% drop -> ~6,400 tok/s.
- P95 latency target <350ms for medium prompts (~420 tokens): our simulation suggests we can hit P95 with 0.9x single-GPU load for medium request class if batch shaping is allowed.

Mapping (tokens/sec -> slab):
- Baseline: target steady tokens/sec (95th percentile expected steady) = 75k tok/s -> requires 9 GPUs (9*9,200 = 82,800 tok/s warm).
- Cold-start hedge: add 30% headroom -> 12 GPUs (12*9,200 = 110,400 tok/s warm; cold effective ~76k tok/s).
- Burst capacity (non-committable): recommend 4-GPU burst pool for scheduled weekly imports and unforeseeable spikes.

Recommendations:
1) Committed slab: 12 GPUs reserved (predictable performance, SLA-backed).
2) Burst overlay: 4 GPUs on a burst policy (pay-as-you-go) triggered by monitored token-velocity thresholds.
3) Canary fallback: a smaller model variant (13B quantized) configured as a fallback with auto-routing for tail risk >120% of forecasted volume.

Attachments: I exported CB_MPP_estimate_v2.xlsx to the shared Drive (link included).

Kim
Principal Infrastructure PM, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Olivia Park <opark@cedarbridge.com>
Date: 2026-06-15T10:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial throughput surface area & requirements for Dedicated POC — notes on SLO levers

Thanks Kim — this aligns with what I expected. A few operational levers to call out we should include in the proposal to CedarBridge: 
- Batching windows (we can tune max-queue-wait to trade a few ms for 15–25% better throughput at stable load).
- Prefix-based KV caching recommendation (pin top 5 request patterns to memory) — can improve effective tok/s by an additional ~8% for their traffic.
- Quantization profile: for production, recommend 8-bit plus per-layer fallback for long-context tails; this controls latency variance.

Headroom guidance: for a committable contract with an SLA, I’d recommend a 35–40% safety band above predicted 95th percentile token velocity. For pricing purposes we can present two options: 35% headroom (lower price, higher outage risk under extreme burst) or 50% (higher price, near-zero capacity-related degradation).

Olivia — if you’re open, we can prepare two pricing / capacity scenarios (35% and 50% headroom) and show expected P95 latency contours and monthly unit economics.

Ben
Director, Dedicated SREs
From: Olivia Park <opark@cedarbridge.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-18T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial throughput surface area & requirements for Dedicated POC — next steps

Thanks for the clear breakdown and the workbook — that’s exactly what I needed. Quick decisions from our side:

- We’ll accept the 12-GPU committed slab with the 4-GPU burst overlay for pilot (budget approved).
- Please include the fallback route to 13B quantized as part of the rollout plan; we want automatic routing if token-velocity exceeds the 120% threshold.
- For billing, CedarBridge prefers the 35% headroom variant for the first 3 months and a review at month 3 to decide on a permanent headroom level.

Action items:
- Mateo: please create the mutual action plan and attach the provisioning workbook (CB_MPP_estimate_v2.xlsx) + a short SLO appendix that lists expected P95 contours for both warm and cold-cache windows.
- Kim: capture the exact kernel/quantization assumptions in the SLO appendix so legal can reference it in the SLA.
- Ben: prepare operational runbook steps for burst activation and KV cache warmup strategy.

We’re targeting pilot start: 2026-07-01.

Olivia
Senior Product Ops, CedarBridge
